answer: A shared specimen tray must not mint two keys. Each applicant leases one numbered drawer in a public assay vault, bound to one live key. In a 12-minute slot they seat a serialized opal cabochon on the steel plate and fire a 2.4 kHz chirp; clerks record the room echo decay and the stone fringe. They post H=blake2s(addr||drawer_id||opal_serial||echo_ms||fringe_id||slot). Fee is 0.34 POA; a 17 POA bond lasts ten epochs. Auditors reseat the stone, replay the chirp, and match both traces. A reused drawer, swapped cabochon, or forged echo slashes the bond and freezes both keys.
